lessons.title: Reciprocal trigonometric functions
lessons.summary: Read reciprocal graphs, locate their undefined angles and solve equations using sine, cosine or tangent.
lessons.objective: Use the reciprocal definitions and identities with the correct angles, signs and domains.
lessons.before: Recall the graphs and special values of sine, cosine and tangent.
lessons.ideas:
The denominators of \(\sec x\), \(\operatorname{cosec}x\) and \(\cot x\) are respectively \(\cos x\), \(\sin x\) and \(\sin x\).

The reciprocal of a non-zero function value keeps its sign. Zeros of a denominator determine the asymptotes.

From the unit-circle identity, \(\sec^2x=1+\tan^2x\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}^2x=1+\cot^2x\) on their domains.
lessons.method:
1. Write the reciprocal as a quotient and mark where the denominator is zero.
  2. Choose an identity or isolate the ordinary trigonometric function.
  3. Find every angle on the given interval and check the original denominator.
mistakes: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine. Inverse sine returns an angle.
Cotangent is defined when sine is non-zero, including angles at which cosine vanishes.
Choose the sign of a reciprocal from the same denominator.

examples.title: Exact reciprocal
examples.question: Evaluate \(\sec\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\).
examples.solution: Cosine is \(-\frac12\) at the given angle. Its reciprocal is \(-2\).

examples.title: Asymptote in the interval
examples.question: Give the vertical asymptote of \(y=\operatorname{cosec}x\) on \(0
examples.solution: Sine is zero at \(x=\pi\). The excluded endpoints are not inside the interval.

examples.title: Select a quadrant sign
examples.question: Given \(\tan x=\frac{8}{15}\) in quadrant III, find \(\sec x\).
examples.solution: \(\sec^2 x=1+\tan^2x=\frac{289}{225}\). Cosine is negative, so \(\sec x=-\frac{17}{15}\).

lessons.title: Compound angle formulae
lessons.summary: Expand the sine, cosine and tangent of a sum or difference and evaluate exact angles.
lessons.objective: Select and apply the appropriate addition or subtraction formula, with the correct signs.
lessons.before: Know the exact sine, cosine and tangent of the standard angles.
lessons.ideas:
Each formula has two individual angles and a choice of sign. Pay particular attention to the opposite sign between products in cosine.

The tangent formula has the opposite sign in its denominator. Use it where the individual tangents and the resulting quotient are defined.
lessons.method:
1. Select sine, cosine or tangent and identify the two angles.
  2. Substitute exact values, retaining the signs given by the quadrants.
  3. Simplify radicals or collect like trigonometric terms.
mistakes: Sine of a sum uses products of unlike functions.
Cosine of a sum subtracts the product of the sines.
Check the denominator before using the tangent formula.

examples.title: Recognise the sign
examples.question: Find \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\) in terms of \(x\).
examples.solution: The difference formula gives \(1\cdot\cos x-0\cdot\sin x=\cos x\).

examples.title: Tangent of complementary angles
examples.question: What happens to the denominator of the tangent formula for \(\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{3}\)?
examples.solution: The two tangents multiply to one. The denominator is zero, and the tangent of the resulting right angle is undefined.

lessons.title: Double angle formulae
lessons.summary: Choose the double-angle identity that fits the other terms, then solve the resulting equation.
lessons.objective: Use the identities for twice an angle to evaluate exactly and reduce equations to a single trigonometric function.
lessons.before: Recall the compound-angle formulae and the unit-circle identity.
lessons.ideas:
The double-angle formulae come from using the same angle twice.

The two single-square versions of \(\cos 2x\) allow you to work with either sine or cosine.

If a single-angle term may be zero, factorise rather than cancelling it.
lessons.method:
1. Look for a double angle or a product of sine and cosine.
  2. Rewrite using a formula that matches the other terms.
  3. If there is an equation, solve every factor and then enforce the interval.
mistakes: The double-angle cosine has equivalent forms with different signs.
Keep a factor even if it may vanish.
A doubled tangent can be undefined when the original tangent is defined.

examples.title: Cosine only
examples.question: Write \(2-\cos 2x\) in terms of squared cosine.
examples.solution: Replace the doubled cosine by \(2\cos^2x-1\) to obtain \(3-2\cos^2x\).

examples.title: Double tangent and exact sign
examples.question: Given \(\tan x=\frac14\), find \(\tan 2x\).
examples.solution: The quotient has numerator \(\frac12\) and denominator \(\frac{15}{16}\). Thus \(\tan 2x=\frac8{15}\).

lessons.title: The R form
lessons.summary: Combine sine and cosine into one shifted function and use its amplitude, phase and range.
lessons.objective: Find the constants of a sine or cosine R form and interpret the result on a stated interval.
lessons.before: Recall how to expand a sine or cosine of a sum or difference.
lessons.ideas:
Expanding the required target form tells you which coefficient corresponds to cosine of the phase and which corresponds to sine.

The positive amplitude is the square root of the sum of the squares of the coefficients.

The phase changes the angle interval. A restricted interval may not reach the full amplitude.
lessons.method:
1. Expand the required sine or cosine form.
  2. Match coefficients, square and add to find the amplitude, then determine the phase with the correct sign.
  3. Convert the interval before solving or locating extrema.
mistakes: The subtraction sign within a cosine gives a positive sine coefficient.
Check that the phase and sign match the requested form.
On a short interval, use endpoint and interior turning values.

examples.title: Match sine first
examples.question: Write \(4\sin x+4\cos x\) in sine R form.
examples.solution: Both coefficient magnitudes are \(4\), so \(R=4\sqrt2\) and \(\alpha=\frac{\pi}{4}\). The form is \(4\sqrt2\sin(x+\frac{\pi}{4})\).

examples.title: Match cosine first
examples.question: Write \(5\cos x-5\sin x\) in cosine R form.
examples.solution: The negative sine coefficient matches plus inside the cosine argument. The form is \(5\sqrt2\cos(x+\frac{\pi}{4})\).

examples.title: Translate the output
examples.question: Find the maximum of \(3+7\cos(x-\frac{\pi}{5})\) over a whole cycle.

lessons.title: Further trigonometric equations and identities
lessons.summary: Choose a useful identity, preserve the domain and find every solution on the original interval.
lessons.objective: Prove identities one side at a time and solve equations involving fractions, squares or transformed arguments.
lessons.before: Recall the reciprocal, compound-angle and double-angle identities.
lessons.ideas:
For an identity, start with one expression and show how it equals the other wherever the original expressions are defined.

For an equation, first write domain restrictions. Reduce to one function or a factorised product and solve every admissible branch.

Map both bounds to any substituted argument, including endpoint inclusion. After returning to the original variable, check the original equation.
lessons.method:
1. Write the domain and select a simplification.
  2. Solve all admissible factor or function branches.
  3. Check original units, bounds and any excluded angles.
mistakes: Cancelling a factor does not remove an original restriction.
A quadratic in cosine may have algebraic roots outside the range from minus one to one.
Each cycle in the transformed interval can add roots.

examples.title: Prove a simple quotient identity
examples.question: Simplify \(\frac{1-\cos^2x}{\sin x}\) where defined.
examples.solution: Rewrite the numerator as \(\sin^2x\). Cancelling on the original domain gives \(\sin x\) for \(\sin x\ne0\).

examples.title: Transform the bounds
examples.question: Put \(u=3x-\frac{\pi}{4}\) when \(0\le x<\frac{\pi}{2}\). Give the bounds for \(u\).
examples.solution: Apply the same transformation to both endpoints. The interval is \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\le u<\frac{5\pi}{4}\).

examples.title: Reject a trigonometric output
examples.question: Can \(2\cos x=3\) have a real solution?
examples.solution: It would require \(\cos x=\frac32\), outside the range of cosine. There is no real solution.

questions.title: Evaluate two reciprocals
questions.prompt_html: Find the exact values of \(\sec\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
Find the underlying values first. \(\cos\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right)=- \frac{1}{2}\) and \(\sin\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right)=- \frac{1}{2}\).

Take the reciprocal of each. Each reciprocal has the same sign as its denominator.
questions.hint_html: Use the reference angle and quadrant for the denominator of each function.

questions.title: Evaluate two reciprocals
questions.prompt_html: Find the exact values of \(\sec\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
Find the underlying values first. \(\cos\left(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\right)=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) and \(\sin\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\).

Take the reciprocal of each. Each reciprocal has the same sign as its denominator.
questions.hint_html: Use the reference angle and quadrant for the denominator of each function.

questions.title: Locate every vertical asymptote
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=\sec(2x)\) on \(0\le x<\pi\), give every \(x\)-coordinate of a vertical asymptote.
questions.solution_html:
The asymptotes are where \(\cos(2x)=0\). The interval for \(2x\) is \(0\le 2x<2 \pi\).

The zeros in that interval occur at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\). Divide each by \(2\).
questions.hint_html: Set the denominator equal to zero in the interval for the multiplied angle.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all asymptote x-values in radians.

questions.title: Locate every vertical asymptote
questions.prompt_html: For \(y=\operatorname{cosec}(3x)\) on \(0\le x<\pi\), give every \(x\)-coordinate of a vertical asymptote.
questions.solution_html:
The asymptotes are where \(\sin(3x)=0\). The interval for \(3x\) is \(0\le 3x<3 \pi\).

The zeros in that interval occur at \(0\), \(\pi\), \(2 \pi\). Divide each by \(3\).
questions.hint_html: Set the denominator equal to zero in the interval for the multiplied angle.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of cosecant.
Complete correct response for exact value of cosine.

questions.title: Choose the reciprocal sign
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\cot x=- \frac{4}{3}\) and that the terminal arm of \(x\) lies in quadrant II, find the exact values of \(\operatorname{cosec} x\) and \(\cos x\).
questions.solution_html:
Use \(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x=1+\cot^2x=\frac{25}{9}\). Sine has the positive sign in quadrant II, so \(\operatorname{cosec} x=\frac{5}{3}\).

Use \(\cos x=\cot x\sin x\) with \(\sin x=\frac{3}{5}\).
questions.hint_html: The square determines a magnitude. Use the quadrant to select the sign.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of cosecant.

questions.title: Choose the reciprocal sign
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\cot x=- \frac{5}{12}\) and that the terminal arm of \(x\) lies in quadrant IV, find the exact values of \(\operatorname{cosec} x\) and \(\cos x\).
questions.solution_html:
Use \(\operatorname{cosec}^2 x=1+\cot^2x=\frac{169}{144}\). Sine has the negative sign in quadrant IV, so \(\operatorname{cosec} x=- \frac{13}{12}\).

Use \(\cos x=\cot x\sin x\) with \(\sin x=- \frac{12}{13}\).
questions.hint_html: The square determines a magnitude. Use the quadrant to select the sign.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Solve a reciprocal equation
questions.prompt_html: Find all exact solutions of \(\sec(2x)=-2\) for \(- \frac{\pi}{2}\le x<\pi\).
questions.solution_html:
Take reciprocals to give \(\cos(2x)=- \frac{1}{2}\). Work in \(- \pi\le 2x<2 \pi\).

In that interval the multiplied angles are \(- \frac{2 \pi}{3}\), \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\), \(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\). Divide each by \(2\) to recover \(x\).
questions.hint_html: Write the transformed interval before listing sine or cosine solutions.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Solve a reciprocal equation
questions.prompt_html: Find all exact solutions of \(\operatorname{cosec}(2x)=2\) for \(0\le x<\frac{3 \pi}{2}\).
questions.solution_html:
Take reciprocals to give \(\sin(2x)=\frac{1}{2}\). Work in \(0\le 2x<3 \pi\).

In that interval the multiplied angles are \(\frac{\pi}{6}\), \(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\), \(\frac{13 \pi}{6}\), \(\frac{17 \pi}{6}\). Divide each by \(2\) to recover \(x\).
questions.hint_html: Write the transformed interval before listing sine or cosine solutions.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of sine.
Complete correct response for exact value of cosine.

questions.title: Evaluate a compound sine and cosine
questions.prompt_html: Use compound angle formulae to find the exact values of \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) and \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
\[\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\]

\[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}=- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\]
questions.hint_html: The sine formula has the same sign between products as between angles. The cosine formula has the opposite sign.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of sine.
Complete correct response for exact value of cosine.

questions.title: Evaluate a compound sine and cosine
questions.prompt_html: Use compound angle formulae to find the exact values of \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) and \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
\[\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}=- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\]

\[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\]
questions.hint_html: The sine formula has the same sign between products as between angles. The cosine formula has the opposite sign.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of tangent.

questions.title: Use the tangent sum or difference formula
questions.prompt_html: Give the exact value of \(\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
The individual tangents are \(1\), \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\). The denominator in the compound formula is \(1 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\) and is non-zero.

\[\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}{1 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}}=\sqrt{3} + 2\]
questions.hint_html: Use the opposite sign in the denominator of the tangent formula.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of tangent.

questions.title: Use the tangent sum or difference formula
questions.prompt_html: Give the exact value of \(\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
The individual tangents are \(\sqrt{3}\), \(1\). The denominator in the compound formula is \(1 + \sqrt{3}\) and is non-zero.

\[\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{1 + \sqrt{3}}=2 - \sqrt{3}\]
questions.hint_html: Use the opposite sign in the denominator of the tangent formula.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of sine.

questions.title: Recover the missing signs
questions.prompt_html: Angle \(A\) is in quadrant II and \(\sin A=\frac{3}{5}\). Angle \(B\) is in quadrant IV and \(\cos B=\frac{5}{13}\). Find \(\sin\left(A+B\right)\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The unit-circle identity and the quadrants give \(\cos A=- \frac{4}{5}\) and \(\sin B=- \frac{12}{13}\).

\[\sin\left(A+B\right)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B=\frac{63}{65}\]
questions.hint_html: Find and sign the other two trigonometric values before multiplying.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for exact value of sine.

questions.title: Recover the missing signs
questions.prompt_html: Angle \(A\) is in quadrant III and \(\sin A=- \frac{5}{13}\). Angle \(B\) is in quadrant II and \(\cos B=- \frac{4}{5}\). Find \(\sin\left(A-B\right)\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The unit-circle identity and the quadrants give \(\cos A=- \frac{12}{13}\) and \(\sin B=\frac{3}{5}\).

\[\sin\left(A-B\right)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B=\frac{56}{65}\]
questions.hint_html: Find and sign the other two trigonometric values before multiplying.

questions.title: Collect the sine and cosine coefficients
questions.prompt_html: Rewrite \(4\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)-2\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) in the form \(a\cos x+b\sin x\). Give the exact coefficients.
questions.solution_html:
Expand the separate angles to give \(4(\cos x\cos \frac{\pi}{3}-\sin x\sin \frac{\pi}{3})\) and \(2(\sin x\cos \frac{\pi}{6}-\cos x\sin \frac{\pi}{6})\).

Keep the sign between the two brackets when collecting common functions. The cosine coefficient is \(3\) and the sine coefficient is \(- 3 \sqrt{3}\).
questions.hint_html: Expand both functions separately. Keep the full second bracket when there is a minus sign outside it.

questions.title: Collect the sine and cosine coefficients
questions.prompt_html: Rewrite \(2\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+6\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\) in the form \(a\cos x+b\sin x\). Give the exact coefficients.
questions.solution_html:
Expand the separate angles to give \(2(\cos x\cos \frac{\pi}{6}-\sin x\sin \frac{\pi}{6})\) and \(6(\sin x\cos \frac{\pi}{3}-\cos x\sin \frac{\pi}{3})\).

Keep the sign between the two brackets when collecting common functions. The cosine coefficient is \(- 2 \sqrt{3}\) and the sine coefficient is \(2\).
questions.hint_html: Expand both functions separately. Keep the full second bracket when there is a minus sign outside it.

questions.title: Find both double-angle values
questions.prompt_html: The terminal arm of \(x\) lies in quadrant II and \(\cos x=- \frac{5}{13}\). Find \(\sin 2x\) and \(\cos 2x\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The quadrant gives \(\sin x=\frac{12}{13}\). Then \(\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x=- \frac{120}{169}\).

Use \(\cos 2x=2\cos^2 x-1=- \frac{119}{169}\).
questions.hint_html: Work out the sign of sine before using the sine double-angle identity.

questions.title: Find both double-angle values
questions.prompt_html: The terminal arm of \(x\) lies in quadrant III and \(\cos x=- \frac{4}{5}\). Find \(\sin 2x\) and \(\cos 2x\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The quadrant gives \(\sin x=- \frac{3}{5}\). Then \(\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x=\frac{24}{25}\).

Use \(\cos 2x=2\cos^2 x-1=\frac{7}{25}\).
questions.hint_html: Work out the sign of sine before using the sine double-angle identity.

questions.title: Find a double tangent
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\tan x=\frac{3}{2}\), find the exact value of \(\tan 2x\).
questions.solution_html:
Substitute into \(\tan 2x=\frac{2\tan x}{1-\tan^2 x}\).

\[\tan 2x=\frac{3}{- \frac{5}{4}}=- \frac{12}{5}\]
questions.hint_html: The denominator is one minus the square of the original tangent.

questions.title: Find a double tangent
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\tan x=- \frac{2}{5}\), find the exact value of \(\tan 2x\).
questions.solution_html:
Substitute into \(\tan 2x=\frac{2\tan x}{1-\tan^2 x}\).

\[\tan 2x=\frac{- \frac{4}{5}}{\frac{21}{25}}=- \frac{20}{21}\]
questions.hint_html: The denominator is one minus the square of the original tangent.

After expanding the multiplier, the coefficient of the squared term is \(-6\) and the constant is \(8\).

questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\sin 2x=1\cos x\) for \(0\le x<2 \pi\). Give every exact root.
questions.solution_html:
Use \(\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x\) and bring both sides together.

\[\cos x\left(2\sin x-1\right)=0\]

List the solutions of \(\cos x=0\) and \(\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\) in the original interval.

Use \(\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x\) and bring both sides together.

\[\sin x\left(2\cos x-1\right)=0\]

questions.title: Match a cosine R form
questions.prompt_html: Write \(4\cos x+4 \sqrt{3}\sin x\) as \(R\cos\left(x-\alpha\right)\) with \(R>0\) and \(0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}\). Give the exact values of \(R\) and \(\alpha\) in radians.
questions.solution_html:
Expanding \(R\cos\left(x-\alpha\right)\), the coefficient of cosine is \(R\cos\alpha\) and the magnitude of the sine coefficient is \(R\sin\alpha\).

Compare with \(4\cos x+4 \sqrt{3}\sin x\). Squaring and adding the coefficient equations gives \(R=8\). Their ratio gives \(\tan\alpha=\sqrt{3}\), so \(\alpha=\frac{\pi}{3}\).
questions.hint_html: Expand the required cosine form. Its sine coefficient has the opposite sign to the one inside the angle bracket.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for value of r.
Complete correct response for value of α in radians.

questions.title: Match a cosine R form
questions.prompt_html: Write \(3 \sqrt{3}\cos x-3\sin x\) as \(R\cos\left(x+\alpha\right)\) with \(R>0\) and \(0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}\). Give the exact values of \(R\) and \(\alpha\) in radians.
questions.solution_html:
Expanding \(R\cos\left(x+\alpha\right)\), the coefficient of cosine is \(R\cos\alpha\) and the magnitude of the sine coefficient is \(R\sin\alpha\).

Compare with \(3 \sqrt{3}\cos x-3\sin x\). Squaring and adding the coefficient equations gives \(R=6\). Their ratio gives \(\tan\alpha=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\), so \(\alpha=\frac{\pi}{6}\).
questions.hint_html: Expand the required cosine form. Its sine coefficient has the opposite sign to the one inside the angle bracket.

questions.title: Find a sine amplitude and phase
questions.prompt_html: Write \(12\sin x+5\cos x\) as \(R\sin\left(x+\alpha\right)\) with \(R>0\) and \(0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ\). Give \(R\) exactly and \(\alpha\) in degrees to one decimal place.
questions.solution_html:
The sine coefficient gives \(R\cos\alpha=12\) and the magnitude of the cosine coefficient gives \(R\sin\alpha=5\).

Square and add to find \(R=13\). Dividing gives \(\tan\alpha=\frac{5}{12}\) and therefore \(\alpha=22.6^\circ\) to one decimal place.
questions.hint_html: In a sine R form, the coefficient on \(\sin x\) is \(R\cos\alpha\).

fields.label: Value of α in degrees, to 1 decimal place

questions.title: Find a sine amplitude and phase
questions.prompt_html: Write \(4\sin x-7\cos x\) as \(R\sin\left(x-\alpha\right)\) with \(R>0\) and \(0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ\). Give \(R\) exactly and \(\alpha\) in degrees to one decimal place.
questions.solution_html:
The sine coefficient gives \(R\cos\alpha=4\) and the magnitude of the cosine coefficient gives \(R\sin\alpha=7\).

Square and add to find \(R=\sqrt{65}\). Dividing gives \(\tan\alpha=\frac{7}{4}\) and therefore \(\alpha=60.3^\circ\) to one decimal place.
questions.hint_html: In a sine R form, the coefficient on \(\sin x\) is \(R\cos\alpha\).

questions.title: Read amplitude and range
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum and maximum of \(y=5+2 \sqrt{3}\sin x+2\cos x\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\).
questions.solution_html:
The curve is \(y=5+4\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\).

The interval covers one full cycle. The sine reaches both \(-1\) and \(1\), so the range is \(1\le y\le 9\).
questions.hint_html: Keep the vertical offset after using the amplitude to set the extreme values.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for minimum value.
Complete correct response for maximum value.

questions.title: Read amplitude and range
questions.prompt_html: Find the minimum and maximum of \(y=-2+3\sin x-3 \sqrt{3}\cos x\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\).
questions.solution_html:
The curve is \(y=-2+6\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\).

The interval covers one full cycle. The sine reaches both \(-1\) and \(1\), so the range is \(-8\le y\le 4\).
questions.hint_html: Keep the vertical offset after using the amplitude to set the extreme values.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Solve after the phase shift
questions.prompt_html: Find every exact solution of \(6\cos x+6 \sqrt{3}\sin x=6\) on \(- \pi\le x<\pi\).
questions.solution_html:
The left-hand side is \(12\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\). The equation is \(\cos\left(x-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\).

The shifted argument belongs to \(- \frac{4 \pi}{3}\le x-\frac{\pi}{3}<\frac{2 \pi}{3}\). Select \(- \frac{\pi}{3}\), \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), then undo the shift.
questions.hint_html: Match a cosine R form and shift both bounds before finding the solutions.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Solve after the phase shift
questions.prompt_html: Find every exact solution of \(2 \sqrt{3}\cos x-2\sin x=-2\) on \(0\le x<2 \pi\).
questions.solution_html:
The left-hand side is \(4\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\). The equation is \(\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=- \frac{1}{2}\).

The shifted argument belongs to \(\frac{\pi}{6}\le x+\frac{\pi}{6}<\frac{13 \pi}{6}\). Select \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\), \(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\), then undo the shift.
questions.hint_html: Match a cosine R form and shift both bounds before finding the solutions.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Map both endpoints before solving
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\sin\left(3x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\) for \(0\le x<\pi\). Give every exact root.
questions.solution_html:
Set \(u=3x-\frac{\pi}{6}\). The transformed interval is \(- \frac{\pi}{6}\le u<\frac{17 \pi}{6}\).

Within it the equation gives \(\frac{\pi}{6}\), \(\frac{5 \pi}{6}\), \(\frac{13 \pi}{6}\). Convert each using \(x=\frac{u+\frac{\pi}{6}}{3}\).
questions.hint_html: Include every cycle of the transformed interval and preserve its open upper endpoint.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Map both endpoints before solving
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\cos\left(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=- \frac{1}{2}\) for \(- \frac{\pi}{2}\le x<\pi\). Give every exact root.
questions.solution_html:
Set \(u=2x+\frac{\pi}{3}\). The transformed interval is \(- \frac{2 \pi}{3}\le u<\frac{7 \pi}{3}\).

Within it the equation gives \(- \frac{2 \pi}{3}\), \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\), \(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\). Convert each using \(x=\frac{u-\frac{\pi}{3}}{2}\).
questions.hint_html: Include every cycle of the transformed interval and preserve its open upper endpoint.

questions.title: Reject a value outside the function range
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(2 \cos^2 x - 3 \cos x - 2=0\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\). Give all exact roots.
questions.solution_html:
Put \(u=\cos x\). The quadratic is \(2 u^{2} - 3 u - 2=0\). Its roots are \(- \frac{1}{2}\), \(2\).

Reject \(2\) because it is outside \(-1\le u\le 1\). Solve \(\cos x=- \frac{1}{2}\) across the stated interval.
questions.hint_html: Find the two candidate outputs before solving for angles. Check the real range of the function.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Reject a value outside the function range
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(2 \sin^2 x + 5 \sin x - 3=0\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\). Give all exact roots.
questions.solution_html:
Put \(u=\sin x\). The quadratic is \(2 u^{2} + 5 u - 3=0\). Its roots are \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(-3\).

Reject \(-3\) because it is outside \(-1\le u\le 1\). Solve \(\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\) across the stated interval.
questions.hint_html: Find the two candidate outputs before solving for angles. Check the real range of the function.

questions.title: Remove an undefined candidate
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\frac{2 \cos^2 x + \cos x - 1}{\sin x}=0\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\). Give all exact roots.
questions.solution_html:
A zero quotient needs numerator zero and denominator non-zero. Set \(u=\cos x\). The numerator has roots \(-1\), \(\frac{1}{2}\).

\(\cos x=-1\) gives \(x=\pi\), where the original denominator is zero. The allowed roots come from \(\cos x=\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint_html: Solve the numerator and keep only angles where the original denominator is defined and non-zero.

marking_criteria.description_html: Complete correct response for all x-values in radians.

questions.title: Remove an undefined candidate
questions.prompt_html: Solve \(\frac{2 \sin^2 x - \sin x - 1}{\cos x}=0\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\). Give all exact roots.
questions.solution_html:
A zero quotient needs numerator zero and denominator non-zero. Set \(u=\sin x\). The numerator has roots \(1\), \(- \frac{1}{2}\).

\(\sin x=1\) gives \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\), where the original denominator is zero. The allowed roots come from \(\sin x=- \frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint_html: Solve the numerator and keep only angles where the original denominator is defined and non-zero.

questions.title: Use the conjugate expression
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\sec x+\tan x=3\), find \(\sec x\) and \(\tan x\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The reciprocal identity gives \(\left(\sec x+\tan x\right)\left(\sec x-\tan x\right)=1\). Therefore \(\sec x-\tan x=\frac{1}{3}\).

Add the two equations to find \(\sec x\) and subtract them to find \(\tan x\).
questions.hint_html: The product of the two opposite-sign expressions is one.

questions.title: Use the conjugate expression
questions.prompt_html: Given \(\operatorname{cosec} x-\cot x=4\), find \(\operatorname{cosec} x\) and \(\cot x\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The reciprocal identity gives \(\left(\operatorname{cosec} x+\cot x\right)\left(\operatorname{cosec} x-\cot x\right)=1\). Therefore \(\operatorname{cosec} x+\cot x=\frac{1}{4}\).

Add the two equations to find \(\operatorname{cosec} x\) and subtract them to find \(\cot x\).
questions.hint_html: The product of the two opposite-sign expressions is one.

questions.title: Sketch a reciprocal over one cycle
questions.prompt_html:
The function \(f(x)=\sec(2x)\) is considered on \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}\) wherever it is defined.

  1. State the equations of the vertical asymptotes and the coordinates of the \(y\)-intercept. [3]
  2. Sketch the graph. Label its two endpoint values and use the correct asymptotic behaviour. [2]
  3. Solve \(|f(x)|=2\) on this interval. [2]
questions.answer_html:
1. \(x=-\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{4}\); \((0,1)\).
  2. Central branch above the axis with minimum \((0,1)\). Negative outer branches start and end at \((-\frac{\pi}{2},-1)\) and \((\frac{\pi}{2},-1)\).
  3. \(- \frac{\pi}{3}\), \(- \frac{\pi}{6}\), \(\frac{\pi}{6}\), \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
questions.solution_html:
1. The denominator \(\cos(2x)\) vanishes when \(2x=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\). At \(x=0\) it equals \(1\), so the reciprocal is \(1\).

  2. The cosine is positive between the asymptotes. The central secant branch rises to positive infinity at either end. The cosine is negative on the two outer branches. Those secant branches tend to negative infinity at the asymptotes.

    At either endpoint \(2x=\pm\pi\), the cosine and reciprocal are both \(-1\). The graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis.

  3. The levels \(\sec(2x)=\pm 2\) correspond to \(\cos(2x)=\pm\frac12\). In \(-\pi\le 2x\le\pi\), this gives \(2x=\pm\frac{\pi}{3},\ \pm\frac{2\pi}{3}\).

    Divide all four angles by two.
questions.hint_html: Identify the zeros and signs of the denominator before drawing the reciprocal.

marking_criteria.description_html: Set \(\cos(2x)=0\) on the transformed interval.
Give both vertical asymptotes.
Give the intercept \((0,1)\).
Sketch the central branch with appropriate asymptotic ends.
Sketch both negative branches with the two labelled endpoint values.
Use both levels and convert to cosine.
Give all four angles and no extra roots.

questions.title: Cotangent over three periods
questions.prompt_html:
The equation \(\cot^2(2x)+\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}\cot(2x)-1=0\) is to be solved for \(0

  1. Find the two possible values of \(\cot(2x)\) exactly. [2]
  2. Find every exact value of \(x\) in the stated interval. [4]
questions.solution_html:
1. Write \(u=\cot(2x)\). The left-hand side factors as \((u-\frac{\sqrt3}{3})(u+\sqrt3)\). The two zeros give the required cotangents.

  2. The interval for \(2x\) is \(0<2x\le3\pi\). The positive cotangent is at \(2x=\frac{\pi}{3},\frac{4\pi}{3},\frac{7\pi}{3}\). The negative cotangent is at \(2x=\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{11\pi}{6},\frac{17\pi}{6}\).

    Divide the six results by two. None makes \(\sin(2x)\) zero.
questions.hint_html: Cotangent has period \(\pi\). Count periods in the interval for \(2x\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Solve the quadratic in \(\cot(2x)\).
Give both exact values.
Map the interval to \(2x\).
Use both cotangent branches and add integer multiples of \(\pi\).
Give the three positive-cotangent roots.
Give the three negative-cotangent roots and no additional roots.

questions.title: Use both signs of a reciprocal identity
questions.prompt_html:
Suppose \(\operatorname{cosec}x-\cot x=3\) and \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\).

  1. Without first finding \(x\), determine \(\operatorname{cosec}x+\cot x\). [2]
  2. Find the exact values of \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\). [2]
  3. Determine \(x\) to one decimal place. [2]
questions.solution_html:
1. The product of the two expressions is \(\operatorname{cosec}^2x-\cot^2x=1\). Divide by \(3\) to find the other factor.

  2. Adding and subtracting the two equations gives \(\operatorname{cosec}x=\frac53\) and \(\cot x=-\frac43\). The sine is the reciprocal of the cosecant, and the cosine is cotangent times sine.

  3. The sine is positive and the cosine is negative, which selects quadrant II. Use \(x=180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac35\right)\).
questions.hint_html: The difference of two squares gives a product equal to one.

marking_criteria.description_html: Apply the difference of squares and the reciprocal identity.
Give the other factor exactly.

Give the degree solution to one decimal place.

questions.title: Exact values near half a turn
questions.prompt_html:
Write \(\frac{11\pi}{12}\) as \(\frac{3\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{6}\).

  1. Use a compound angle formula to find \(\sin\left(\frac{11\pi}{12}\right)\) exactly. [2]
  2. Find the exact cosine of the same angle. [2]
  3. Hence express the tangent of the angle in the form \(a+b\sqrt3\) with integers \(a\) and \(b\). [3]
questions.solution_html:
1. Use the sum formula with sine and cosine of the two angles.

    \[\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\left(-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\cdot\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}\]

  2. The cosine sum formula subtracts the product of the sines.

    \[\left(-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac12=-\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}\]

  3. Divide the sine by the cosine. Cancel \(\sqrt2\) before rationalising:

    \[-\frac{\sqrt3-1}{\sqrt3+1}=-\frac{(\sqrt3-1)^2}{3-1}=-2+\sqrt3\]
questions.hint_html: Keep the cosine of \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) negative in each substitution.

Give \(-2+\sqrt3\).

questions.title: Recover the quadrant of a compound angle
questions.prompt_html:
Angle \(A\) lies in quadrant II and \(\sin A=\frac45\). Angle \(B\) lies in quadrant IV and \(\cos B=\frac{12}{13}\).

  1. Find \(\cos A\) and \(\sin B\) exactly. [2]
  2. Find \(\sin(A+B)\) and \(\cos(A+B)\). State the quadrant containing the terminal arm of \(A+B\). [3]
  3. Find \(\tan(A-B)\) exactly. [2]
questions.solution_html:
1. Use the unit-circle identity to determine each magnitude. Cosine is negative in quadrant II and sine is negative in quadrant IV.

  2. The sine sum is \(\frac{48}{65}+\frac{15}{65}=\frac{63}{65}\). The cosine sum is \(-\frac{36}{65}+\frac{20}{65}=-\frac{16}{65}\). This positive sine and negative cosine select quadrant II.

  3. The sine difference is \(\frac{48}{65}-\frac{15}{65}=\frac{33}{65}\). The cosine difference is \(-\frac{36}{65}-\frac{20}{65}=-\frac{56}{65}\). Their quotient is \(-\frac{33}{56}\).
questions.hint_html: Use the signs of the resulting sine and cosine to identify the quadrant of the sum.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give the correct signed cosine.
Give the correct signed sine.
Apply the sine and cosine sum formulae.
Give both exact values.

questions.title: Two shifted terms with a cancellation
questions.prompt_html:
Let \(F(x)=2\cos(x+60^\circ)+2\sin(x+30^\circ)\).

  1. Expand the cosine term and sine term separately in terms of \(\cos x\) and \(\sin x\). [2]
  2. Simplify \(F(x)\) and state its period, in degrees. [2]
  3. Solve \(F(x)=-\sqrt3\) for \(-180^\circ\le x<270^\circ\). [3]
questions.answer_html:
1. \(\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x\) and \(\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x\).
  2. \(F(x)=2\cos x\). Period \(360^\circ\).
  3. \(-150^\circ,\ 150^\circ,\ 210^\circ\).
questions.solution_html:
1. Use the cosine sum formula with \(\cos60^\circ=\frac12\) and \(\sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\). For the sine sum use \(\cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\) and \(\sin30^\circ=\frac12\).

  2. The two sine terms cancel. The coefficient on cosine is two, which scales the values and leaves the cosine period unchanged.

  3. The cosine is \(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\). One cycle gives \(150^\circ\) and \(210^\circ\). Subtracting \(360^\circ\) from \(210^\circ\) gives the additional allowed angle \(-150^\circ\).
questions.hint_html: After expanding, compare the two sine coefficients before solving.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give the correct cosine expansion.
Give the correct sine expansion.
Show the cancellation and give \(2\cos x\).

Reduce to a cosine equation with correct output.
Find both positive roots.

questions.title: When does a doubled tangent exist?
questions.prompt_html:
Suppose \(\tan x=-\frac34\).

  1. Write \(\sin 2x\) and \(\cos 2x\) in terms of \(t=\tan x\). [2]
  2. Find the exact values of \(\sin 2x\), \(\cos 2x\) and \(\tan 2x\). [2]
  3. For which real values of \(t\) is \(\tan 2x\) undefined when \(\tan x=t\) exists? [2]
questions.solution_html:
1. Start with \(2\sin x\cos x\) and \(\cos^2x-\sin^2x\). Divide numerator and denominator of each by \(\cos^2x\) after inserting \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\) as its denominator.

  2. Here \(1+t^2=\frac{25}{16}\) and \(1-t^2=\frac7{16}\). Substituting gives \(\sin 2x=-\frac{24}{25}\) and \(\cos 2x=\frac7{25}\). Their quotient is \(-\frac{24}{7}\).

  3. A doubled tangent is undefined when \(\cos 2x=0\). The denominator \(1+t^2\) is positive. Its numerator is zero exactly when \(t^2=1\).
questions.hint_html: The double-angle sine and cosine can both be expressed using \(\tan x\) by dividing by \(\cos^2x\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the double-angle identities and divide by \(\cos^2x\).
Obtain both rational forms.
Find the correct sine and cosine values.
Find the correct tangent value.

Give both values of \(t\).

questions.title: A root lost by division
questions.prompt_html:
Solve \(\sin 2x=\cos x\) on \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x<\frac{3\pi}{2}\).

  1. Use a double-angle identity to obtain a product equal to zero. [2]
  2. Find all exact solutions in the given interval. [3]
  3. Identify the solutions that would be lost by dividing the starting equation by \(\cos x\). [1]
questions.solution_html:
1. Write \(\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x\), bring the right-hand side across and extract the common factor \(\cos x\).

  2. From \(\cos x=0\) obtain \(x=-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\). From \(\sin x=\frac12\) obtain \(x=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6}\). The angle \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) is excluded by the upper bound.

  3. At these two angles \(\cos x=0\) and \(\sin 2x=0\). They solve the original equation, but division by cosine is undefined there.
questions.hint_html: Use the product rule for an equation equal to zero. Check whether the interval includes each endpoint.

marking_criteria.description_html: Replace the double-angle sine.
Factorise correctly.
Solve both branches.
Give the cosine-zero solutions with correct endpoints.
Give both sine solutions.
Identify both lost roots and explain the zero-divisor issue.

questions.title: Translate a double-angle expression into a range
questions.prompt_html:
For \(0\le x\le\pi\), let \(G(x)=3\cos 2x+2\cos^2x+1\).

  1. Express \(G(x)\) in the form \(a\cos^2x+b\). [2]
  2. Determine the full range of \(G\) and where its minimum occurs. [3]
  3. Find the exact solutions of \(G(x)=0\). [2]
questions.solution_html:
1. The appropriate double-angle identity is \(\cos 2x=2\cos^2x-1\). Substitute and collect to get \(6\cos^2x-3+2\cos^2x+1=8\cos^2x-2\).

  2. On the interval \(\cos x\) ranges from \(1\) to \(-1\). Its square fills \([0,1]\) and vanishes at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Apply the affine transformation \(8u-2\) to that range.

  3. Solve \(\cos^2x=\frac14\), so \(\cos x=\frac12\) or \(\cos x=-\frac12\). Both branches give one angle on the given interval.
questions.hint_html: Choose the form of \(\cos 2x\) that already matches the other variable term.

questions.title: Use a phase shift to locate extrema
questions.prompt_html:
A periodic output is given by \(F(x)=1+\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x\) for \(0\le x<2\pi\).

  1. Write \(F(x)-1\) as \(R\sin(x+\alpha)\) with \(R>0\) and \(0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}\). Give exact constants. [2]
  2. Find the minimum and maximum of \(F\) and the exact angle where each occurs. [3]
questions.solution_html:
1. The expansion has sine coefficient \(R\cos\alpha\) and cosine coefficient \(R\sin\alpha\). Hence \(R^2=1^2+(\sqrt3)^2=4\) and \(\tan\alpha=\sqrt3\).

  2. The sine takes both extreme values on the given cycle. The minimum occurs when \(x+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{3\pi}{2}\). The maximum occurs when \(x+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Apply the amplitude and vertical shift to the two outputs.
questions.hint_html: The constant shifts the output vertically. The phase shifts the angles of the extrema.

marking_criteria.description_html: Compare the coefficients using the sine sum formula.
Give both exact constants.
Use the shifted angles at which sine is \(\pm1\).
Give both extreme values.

questions.title: Find a level on a shifted cycle
questions.prompt_html:
A signal is modelled by \(F(x)=6+5\cos x-12\sin x\) for \(-90^\circ\le x<270^\circ\).

  1. Write \(F(x)-6\) as \(R\cos(x+\alpha)\), where \(R>0\) and \(0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ\). Give \(\alpha\) to one decimal place. [3]
  2. Find all values of \(x\) for which \(F(x)=12\). Give your answers to one decimal place. [3]
questions.solution_html:
1. The cosine sum gives \(R\cos\alpha=5\) and \(R\sin\alpha=12\). Thus \(R=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=13\) and \(\tan\alpha=\frac{12}{5}\).

  2. Using the unrounded \(\alpha\), put \(u=x+\alpha\). The new interval is \(-90^\circ+\alpha\le u<270^\circ+\alpha\).

    The equation gives \(\cos u=\frac{6}{13}\). Let \(\beta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac6{13}\right)\). The two angles in the transformed interval are \(\beta\) and \(360^\circ-\beta\). Subtract \(\alpha\) from each and round only now.
questions.hint_html: Keep the calculator’s unrounded phase when changing the interval and solving the equation.

questions.title: Find the range on a short interval
questions.prompt_html:
For \(0\le x\le\frac{\pi}{6}\), let \(H(x)=2\cos 2x-2\sqrt3\sin 2x\).

  1. Express \(H(x)\) in the form \(R\cos(2x+\alpha)\) with exact positive constants \(R\) and \(0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}\). [2]
  2. Find the range of \(H\) on the stated interval. [3]
  3. Find the exact solution of \(H(x)=0\) on this interval. [2]
questions.solution_html:
1. Comparing coefficients gives \(R\cos\alpha=2\) and \(R\sin\alpha=2\sqrt3\). Square and add to get \(R=4\). Divide to get \(\tan\alpha=\sqrt3\).

  2. The cosine argument runs from \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) to \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\). Cosine decreases throughout this interval. Its endpoints have outputs \(\frac12\) and \(-\frac12\). Multiply both values by four.

  3. The only zero of cosine within the transformed interval is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). Solve \(2x+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{2}\).
questions.hint_html: Read the cosine outputs from the transformed interval. The interval does not cover a full cycle.

questions.title: An identity with a narrower domain
questions.prompt_html:
Consider \(J(x)=\frac{1-\cos 2x}{\sin 2x}\) for \(0\le x\le2\pi\) wherever the quotient is defined.

  1. List all angles in this interval where \(J\) is undefined. [2]
  2. Show that \(J(x)=\tan x\) on the domain of \(J\). [2]
  3. Solve \(J(x)=\sqrt3\) on the given interval. [2]
questions.solution_html:
1. The denominator is zero at integer multiples of \(\pi\) for \(2x\). The interval for \(2x\) includes both zero and \(4\pi\).

  2. Use the double-angle cosine identity with squared sine in the numerator and the double-angle sine identity in the denominator. Cancelling \(2\sin x\) is valid because it is non-zero throughout the stated domain.

    \[\frac{1-\cos 2x}{\sin 2x}=\frac{2\sin^2x}{2\sin x\cos x}=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\tan x\]

  3. The tangent value is attained at \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) and again after one period \(\pi\). Both angles have non-zero original denominators.
questions.hint_html: Simplify the quotient on its original domain. Apply that domain to the final roots.

questions.title: Solve both branches on a shifted interval
questions.prompt_html:
Let \(Q(x)=4\cos^2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-3\) for \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\le x\le\pi\).

  1. Put \(u=x-\frac{\pi}{6}\). Find the interval for \(u\) and state the two possible values of \(\cos u\) when \(Q(x)=0\). [2]
  2. Find all exact solutions of \(Q(x)=0\). [3]
questions.solution_html:
1. Subtract \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) from each endpoint of the original interval. Rewriting \(Q(x)=0\) gives \(\cos^2u=\frac34\), with two possible signs.

  2. The positive branch gives \(u=-\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{6}\). The negative branch gives the included endpoint \(u=\frac{5\pi}{6}\). Add \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) to each.
questions.hint_html: Squaring hides the sign of the cosine. Solve both possibilities before undoing the phase shift.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give the correct closed interval for \(u\).
Give both possible cosine values.
Find solutions in each branch on the transformed interval.
Convert both positive-branch angles back to \(x\).
Include the exact endpoint solution and no extra roots.

questions.title: Keep the original tangent domain
questions.prompt_html:
The equation \(2\sin x+3\tan x=6\sin x\) is to be solved on \(-\pi\le x<\pi\).

  1. State which angles must be excluded. Show that for the remaining angles the equation is equivalent to \(\sin x(3-4\cos x)=0\). [3]
  2. Find all exact solutions. You may leave any non-standard angle in inverse-trigonometric form. [3]
questions.answer_html:
1. Exclude \(- \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). The equivalent equation is \(\sin x(3-4\cos x)=0\).
  2. \(x=-\pi,\quad x=0,\quad x=\pm\cos^{-1}\left(\frac34\right)\).
questions.solution_html:
1. The tangent denominator is \(\cos x\). It vanishes at \(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) within the interval. Elsewhere multiply by cosine, collect terms on one side, and factor out \(\sin x\).

  2. The sine factor gives \(x=-\pi,0\) with \(x=\pi\) outside the half-open interval. The cosine factor gives \(x=\pm\cos^{-1}(\frac34)\) by the even symmetry of cosine. Each angle respects the original domain.
questions.hint_html: The original denominator controls where you can multiply by cosine. Keep every solution from both factors.

marking_criteria.description_html: Give both excluded angles.
Write tangent as a quotient and multiply by the non-zero cosine.
Obtain the given factorisation.
Solve both factors without division by sine.
Give the complete zero-sine branch respecting both endpoints.
Give the complete cosine branch and no undefined angles.
